feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. The race 1 evidence (entityR2A, score 302.7) supports the 16 mm footprint change. The oval finished 12 of 20 trials after the spread change, but s-bend and slalom still had line_loss_events of about 1 and max_error at the 0.06 m limit in all 40 trials. That pattern points to drift that the array cannot recover from, not to a lack of coverage. Your footprint change is a reasonable test because it adds tape overlap at the edges, but it does not by itself add steering authority. I therefore raised kp and kd and lowered base_speed on the controller side. Once the race reports, use this rule. If s-bend and slalom line_loss_events fall below 1 and max_error drops below 0.06, keep the 16 mm footprint and the geometry as proposed. If line loss stays at 1 or more with max_error at the limit, the footprint is not the cause, so hold the geometry and try a different spread, not a larger footprint, because 16 mm is already the largest size. If oval steering_oscillation stays above 0.2 with the new gain, move the sensors forward, as the 0.2 threshold you set requires. Do not change the lead while line loss is still the main failure.
requested_changes: Keep sensor_size at 0.016 with the ±0.03 m spread and y = 0.05 for the next race, so that the footprint change is tested by itself.

If line_loss_events on s-bend and slalom remain at 1 or more with max_error at 0.06 after the race, try a narrower outer spread of about ±0.025 m with 0.016 footprints, to see whether the outer sensors are reading the tape too late during drift. Do not change the lead.

If oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.2 after the race, move the sensors forward to y = 0.06 to 0.065, keeping the spread and footprint unchanged, so that the lead change is the only geometry change in that race.
